newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Nationalist, leftwinger win Russian regional polls.
newsitem.headline: Nationalist, leftwinger win Russian regional polls.

text.p: A member of Vladimir Zhirinovsky's extreme nationalist Liberal Democratic Party won a seat in Russia's upper house of parliament, defeating the governor appointed earlier by President Boris Yeltsin.

Zhirinovsky, a flamboyant and at times outrageous character, had campaigned actively for Yevgeny Mikhailov in the northwestern region of Pskov, which borders the Baltic former Soviet republic of Estonia.

Russian news agencies, which reported the Pskov result, said on Monday the Kremlin's candidate also lost in Sunday's voting in the remote northeastern region of Magadan, location of many of Soviet-era dictator Josef Stalin's prison camps.
Voters there selected Valentin Tsvetkov, who represented a leftwing bloc of communists and their allies.
The local elections, being held in most of Russia's 89 regions over a six-month period ending in February, give voters a chance to choose a new regional governor.
But the polls are important on a national level as well because the regional governors also become members of the Federation Council upper house of parliament.
Communists and other conservatives already dominate the lower house and they hope for a strong showing in the regional elections to increase their influence in the upper house.
The regional elections held so far this year, have given a clear advantage to neither to the Kremlin nor the communist-led opposition.

Russia has an unresolved border dispute with Estonia in the Pskov region and the Kremlin's relations with the Baltic state, complicated by the presence of a large ethnic Russian minority there, have been troubled.
